bib.title: Long-context LLMs Struggle with Long In-context Learning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "LongICLBench: Long-context LLMs Struggle with Long In-context Learning". Tianle Li, Ge Zhang, Quy Duc Do, Xiang Yue, Wenhu Chen. Affiliations are University of Waterloo, Carnegie Mellon University (Yue) and Vector Institute, Toronto. It is an arXiv preprint (2404.02060v3, cs.CL, 12 Jun 2024). No venue is printed in the PDF.

COVERAGE: All 19 pages and all 64,513 extracted chars were read: body, Tables 1-10, appendix A.1-A.6, and the references (skimmed). Figures were not viewed. Figure content is known only from the text and the captions in the extraction.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: On the hardest task, Discovery (174 labels), nearly every model scores about zero, and only Gemini-1.5-Pro is clearly above zero.
  number: Gemini-1.5-Pro 14.0 at 10K tokens, then 6.0, 3.2, 1.8, 2.8 at 20K to 50K. GPT4-turbo 1.5 at 10K, then 0.5. GPT4o 2.8, Claude3-Opus 1.2. Fine-tuned SoTA is 87.4.
  setup: 500 test examples per dataset, 1 to 5 rounds of demonstrations (1 round is one example per label), and 15 models. Metric is accuracy.
  quote: "On the most difficult extreme-label classification task Discovery (Sileo et al., 2019), all LLMs achieve close-to-zero performance except Gemini-1.5-Pro with 14% accuracy. In contrast, a fine-tuned BERT model (Kenton & Toutanova, 2019) can achieve 87%."
  where: p.3 (intro), Table 6 on p.8.
- Claim: Performance falls as task difficulty (label count and demonstration length) rises, and the strongest models reach a ceiling between DialogRE and Discovery.
  number: none stated as one figure. GPT4-turbo scores 84.4 (BANKING77, 5R), 84.2 (TacRED, 5R), 57.7 (DialogRE, 5R) and 0.5 (Discovery, 5R).
  setup: same as above.
  quote: "Our initial hypothesis suggests that the strongest LLMs like GPT-4-turbo are capped at a certain complexity level between DialogRE and Discovery."
  where: p.6, Tables 3-6.
- Claim: More demonstrations help only up to a point. Most models peak mid-length (about 13K-25K tokens) and then degrade or fluctuate. Only GPT4-turbo and GPT4o consistently improve on TacRED and DialogRE.
  number: Claude3-Opus on BANKING77 goes 62.2 (7K), 43.8 (9K), 26.0 (14K). On TacRED it goes 74.1 (7K), 35.4 (10K). On DialogRE it goes 30.3 (13K), 15.3 (19K), 0.8 (25K), 0 (32K). Mistral on TacRED falls 53.3 to 42.3 from 4K to 18K. Gemini-1.5-Pro on BANKING77 goes 82.2 (7K) to 70.4 (14K).
  setup: as above. These are the paper's cases of late-context degradation.
  quote: "only GPT4-turbo and GPT4o can consistently benefit from more demonstrations, all of the other models reach their peak at the middle with context length around 13K to 25K."
  where: p.6, Tables 3-5.
- Claim: Grouping same-label demonstrations together lowers accuracy for most models, and the drop can be very large. Models handle labels near the end of the prompt best.
  number: On TacRED 3-round (10K tokens), scattered to grouped: Mistral 51.6 to 5.1 (-46.5). Qwen 45.2 to 33.0 (-12.2). GPT4-turbo 79.5 to 59.2 (-20.3). Gemini-1.5-Pro 79.6 to 57.3 (-22.3). ChatGLM3 38.9 to 35.6 (-3.3).
  setup: TacRED, 41 labels x 3 = 123 instances, base models except the API models. LLaMA-2-7B-32K (+2.6) and RWKV (+2.6) rose slightly, at near-zero baselines.
  quote: "even the GPT4-turbo and Gemini1.5-Pro are not immune to the challenges posed by grouped distributions, experiencing a notable decline in performance by 20.3% and 22.3%."
  where: p.9 (section 4.2), Table 10 on p.19.
- Claim: Some models (Mistral, InternLM2) can use only the labels at the end of the prompt once examples are grouped. The abstract describes this as a bias toward later labels.
  number: none beyond Table 10. InternLM2 goes 15.5 to 4.8.
  setup: TacRED, grouped distribution.
  quote: "demonstrate high sensitivity to the distribution of instances, only handling instances with labels positioned at the end of the prompt."
  where: p.9. The abstract on p.1 says "a bias towards labels presented later in the sequence".
- Claim: Non-Transformer models (RWKV, Mamba) perform far behind the Transformers. Mamba-2.8B scores 0 on every task.
  number: RWKV on BANKING77 gets 8.6, 21.2, 0.4, 0, 0. Mamba-2.8B gets 0 on all.
  setup: RWKV-5-World 3B (Table 2 lists 3B; the result tables list 7B) and Mamba-2.8B. Their training windows are only 4K and 2K, though the paper lists the support length as ∞.
  quote: "Among the open-source models, the non-Transformer-based models, like RWKV and Mamba (Peng et al., 2023a; Gu & Dao, 2023), perform far behind the Transformer-based models."
  where: p.3, Tables 3-6.
- Claim: A claimed context window does not guarantee usable long-context ability. Several open models with 100K-200K windows score about zero at 2K-14K tokens.
  number: LLaMA-2-7B-LongLora (100K) scores 0 on every column of BANKING77. Yi-6B-200K goes 25.8, 0, 0, 0, 1.2. InternLM2 (200K) on TacRED falls 29.6 to 8.0. Gemma-7B (8K) is 0 on BANKING77.
  setup: base models, extreme-label ICL.
  quote: none beyond the table rows (Table 3: "LLaMA-2-7B-LongLora 7B 100K 0 0 0 0 0"). The paper does not discuss the cause.
  where: Table 3, p.7.
- Claim: Passkey and needle retrieval and QA are weak tests of long context. Passkey is reported as passed (99%+), and QA can be answered from a short snippet.
  number: "99%+"
  quote: "Several LLMs achieve 99%+ on this synthetic task."
  where: p.2 (intro). The paper cites this without testing it.
- Claim: Some models' accuracy is nearly linear in demonstration length.
  number: none.
  quote: "the performance of Qwen and Mistral is almost linear w.r.t the demonstration length."
  where: p.6.

Other numbers
- Benchmark: 6 datasets, 28 to 174 classes, 2K to 50K tokens (Table 1). The datasets are GoEmotions (28 labels), BANKING77 (77), TacRED (41), Few-NERD (66), DialogRE (36) and Discovery (174).
- Discovery takes 61 tokens per example, so 1 shot per label already exceeds 10K tokens.
- Best scores at 5 rounds, against fine-tuned SoTA: BANKING77 GPT4-turbo 84.4 (SoTA 94.4). TacRED GPT4-turbo 84.2 and Gemini 82.3 (SoTA 76.8, so beaten). DialogRE GPT4-turbo 57.7 (SoTA 77.1). Few-NERD GPT4-turbo 56.8 (SoTA 70.9). GoEmotions GPT4-turbo 32.0 (SoTA 58.9).
- Few-NERD (Table 8) is the one dataset where most Transformer models still improve with length. GoEmotions (Table 7) gets no benefit from more shots.

LIMITS
- Authors concede: "LongICLBench currently encompasses only one type of evaluation application, specifically on extreme-label classification with long in-context learning" (A.6, p.18).
- Only 500 test examples per dataset and a single sampled demonstration set shared by all models. There are no seeds, variance or confidence intervals.
- The position analysis is a pilot on one dataset (TacRED, 3 rounds) and has no controlled position sweep. The "later-label bias" is read off scatter plots.
- Open models are about 7B base models (not instruction-tuned) and the API models are instruction-tuned. This confounds model-class comparisons. Zeros may partly reflect the models failing the output format, not a lack of understanding, and the paper does not separate the two.
- Table 6 marks some cells ✗ (out of memory or over-length, not explained).
- Dated: the models are GPT-4-turbo, GPT-4o, Claude 3 Opus and Gemini-1.5-Pro as of spring 2024. Newer models are not covered. The causal "reasoning" explanation in the abstract is asserted without an experiment.
- The Table 2/Table 3 labels for RWKV differ (3B versus 7B), and its support length is listed as 4K in some tables and 1K in others.

BUILDS ON
- Lost in the Middle (Liu et al., 2023) for the position analysis.
- Extreme-label ICL (Anil et al., 2022; Milios et al., 2023).
- Datasets: Demszky 2020, Casanueva 2020, Zhang 2017, Ding 2021, Yu 2020, Sileo 2019.
- Related long-context benchmarks: LongBench (Bai 2023b), L-Eval (An 2023), LooGLE (Li 2023b), ∞Bench (Zhang 2024), Long-Range Arena (Tay 2021), and passkey (Mohtashami & Jaggi 2023).
- Context-extension methods: RoPE (Su), ALiBi (Press), Position Interpolation (Chen 2023a), LongLoRA, LongRoPE (Ding 2024), Mamba (Gu & Dao 2023), RWKV (Peng 2023a).

CODE: none. The prompt templates are in Table 9 on p.18: "Given a customer service query, please predict the intent of the query. The predicted answer must come from the demonstration examples with the exact format."

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.1): accuracy against context length per model across difficulty levels. It shows the rise-then-fall pattern.
- Fig 2 (p.2): passkey and QA tasks versus extreme-label ICL. It shows why the benchmark needs the whole prompt.
- Fig 3 (p.3): representative models across datasets at 9K, 18K, 32K and 41K tokens.
- Fig 4 (p.9): per-class accuracy against prompt position, scattered versus grouped. It is the best visual for the position effect.
- Figs 5-6: the same plots for other models.
